what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/paid-access: who holds paid access now (from the person's payment events, offers and grants), whether a buyer may open one gated thing, giving people access by hand (and ending it), and selling a file so only a buyer who holds its access gets it. Every gate asks the one answer of who-holds-access; the file's own paid-file record is its gate; the key is named in rows and handed only on a private pipe.

payload.label: See who holds paid access
payload.job: Work out which paid access one buyer holds right now: what they bought, what renewed, what ended or was refunded, and what I gave them by hand
payload.description: Folds the buyer's payment events (the payment-event records the payment tools keep, which your AI reads from your stores and hands in) through your access-effect-rule rows into effects, folds those into purchase episodes (a purchase starts one, a renewal keeps it, a cancellation or refund ends it) and answers the access refs of the offers they hold now, with every offer that asks for no money held by everyone, plus the access-grant records you wrote for them (a gift, a pass with an end date). Returns held_access_refs (the one list every gate here asks), the episodes behind it, any allowance limits, and problems (events that gave no effect, and why). Give the buyer the way your rules name them; the starter rules read the buyer's email address from the payment event. Without your own rules or lifecycle row it reads the event kinds the payment tool writes. It reads and keeps no records and sends nothing: the rows come in the request, the answer is the whole result.

subject.description: The buyer, the way your access rules name a buyer (the starter rules: their email address)

email_verified.description: Whether the subject's email is verified, as the door read it from the session. false: purchases (which name their buyer by email) give nothing and only grants count. Left out is false: only grants count

payment_events.description: The buyer's payment-event rows (read them from your records first)

offers.description: Your offers (id, access_refs, price_options, allowances): the commercial-offer rows

grants.description: Your access-grant rows (grants and revokes) for the buyer

rules.description: Your access-effect-rule rows; left out or empty, the starter rules for the payment tool's event kinds

lifecycle.description: Your one effect-lifecycle row (episode_keys and transitions); left out, the starter lifecycle

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/signed-event-effects (the rule projection), capability-effect-lifecycle (the fold) and product-access (the grant projection), over the payment events the payment tools keep

record_model._what: The record kinds, indexes and links this tool keeps (moved unchanged from trillion-rust's one record model: src/record_model_policy/record-model.json, src/record_indexes/record-indexes.json, product/lists.json field_kinds and product/record-sharing.json links).

payload.label: Check a buyer may open something
payload.job: Decide whether a buyer may open one gated thing (a page, a lesson, a publication) from the access it requires
payload.description: Takes the scope the thing is gated by ({ schema: "addressed-expiring-value-scope/v1", value_ref, instance_ref, required_access_refs }) and the buyer. A thing that requires no access is open to any named buyer; otherwise the buyer must hold any one of the required access refs now (tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works that out from the access rows the request carries: payment_events, offers, grants, rules, lifecycle). Answers authorized true or false: a scope that is not exactly that schema, no buyer, or access that cannot be worked out is false with no revision. Otherwise the answer carries membership_revision, which changes when the buyer's access changes, so an action admitted on it can fail closed when membership moves.

subject.description: The buyer, the way your access rules name a buyer

email_verified.description: Whether the subject's email is verified, as the door read it from the session. false: purchases give nothing and only grants count. Left out is false: only grants count

payment_events.description: The buyer's payment-event rows (read them from your records first)

offers.description: Your offers (id, access_refs, price_options, allowances): the commercial-offer rows

grants.description: Your access-grant rows (grants and revokes) for the buyer

rules.description: Your access-effect-rule rows; left out or empty, the starter rules

lifecycle.description: Your one effect-lifecycle row; left out, the starter lifecycle

membership_revision.description: membership-revision:ungated for a thing that requires nothing, else a hash of what the buyer holds; it changes when a grant, revoke, payment or refund changes it

payload.label: Seal a paid file
payload.job: Put a file I sell (a book, an audiobook, a course video) behind paid access so only buyers can open it
payload.description: Encrypts one of the person's files with their paid-files key (AES-256-CTR, a fresh nonce per file), keeps the sealed copy in their files, and answers the file's paid-file row: the name buyers ask for it by, the sealed copy's identity, how it is sealed, the key's NAME and the access refs a buyer must hold (any one of them opens it). The key is handed to this run on a private pipe and is never in the row or the answer. This tool keeps no record: store the row it answers, and hand it back as paid_file to tool:give-a-buyer-a-paid-file-link and tool:open-a-paid-file-for-a-buyer.

file.description: The file to sell, in your files (1f: then 64 hex), as find_file or list_files returns it

object_key.description: The name buyers ask for the file by, like "chapter-one.pdf"

required_access_refs.description: The access refs your offers grant; a buyer holding any one opens the file, like ["access:course-a"]

ttl_seconds.description: How long one link to it stays good (3600 when left out)

object_store_ref.description: Which of your stores the file is kept in ("object-store:paid-files" when left out)

provenance.source: bitfield-packages packages/material-delivery (tools/encrypt-private-object.mjs), with the key kept out of the row

replies.body: Made-up chapter one text for a sample file.

payload.label: Give a buyer a paid file link
payload.job: Give a buyer a short-lived link to a file they paid for, and refuse anyone who has not paid
payload.description: Takes the file's paid-file row (as tool:seal-a-paid-file answered it) and answers grant with a link that expires (the record's ttl_seconds, else 3600), only when the subject is a verified account and holds any of the file's required access refs now (worked out as tool:see-who-holds-paid-access works it out, from the access rows the request carries). Otherwise answers denied (anonymous, not-entitled) or unavailable (no sealed bytes, no such file, access could not be worked out). The file's gate comes from its paid-file row, never from the buyer. It keeps nothing. subject must be the account the door verified from the buyer's own session. The link carries no bytes and no key; every open is checked again by tool:open-a-paid-file-for-a-buyer.

object_key.description: The file the buyer asks for, like "chapter-one.pdf"

paid_file.description: The file's paid-file row: the row answer of tool:seal-a-paid-file, as your records keep it

subject.description: The account the door verified from the buyer's session, named the way your access rules name a buyer; empty for no session

email_verified.description: Whether the subject's email is verified, as the door read it from the session. Only true lets purchases give access; false or left out, only grants count

payment_events.description: The buyer's payment-event rows (read them from your records first)

offers.description: Your offers (id, access_refs, price_options, allowances): the commercial-offer rows

grants.description: Your access-grant rows (grants and revokes) for the buyer

rules.description: Your access-effect-rule rows; left out or empty, the starter rules

lifecycle.description: Your one effect-lifecycle row; left out, the starter lifecycle

payload.label: Open a paid file for a buyer
payload.job: Check, each time a buyer opens a paid file link, that they still hold access, and say which sealed bytes to stream
payload.description: For a link's token and the account presenting it: refuses a malformed or expired token, then checks the file's paid-file row against what the presenter holds now (from the access rows the request carries), so a refund or an ended subscription stops the very next open and a link passed to someone else does not open. On authorized it answers the sealed copy's identity, the cipher, the nonce and the NAME of the key the door decrypts with; never the key.

token.description: The last part of the link the buyer opened

paid_file.description: The paid-file row of the file the token names: the row answer of tool:seal-a-paid-file, as your records keep it

subject.description: The account the door verified from the presenting session, named the way your access rules name a buyer

email_verified.description: Whether the subject's email is verified, as the door read it from the session. Only true lets purchases give access; false or left out, only grants count
